summary.text: Slack supports third-party OAuth flows, enabling external apps to be installed on customers' workspaces.
Any developer can register a Slack App via the Slack API portal and request scopes for reading channel history and posting messages.
Commercial distribution to external customers requires either an unlisted app for pilots or an approved listing in the Slack Marketplace.

claims.text: Third-party OAuth is supported by Slack via standard OAuth 2.0 authorization code flows allowing external apps to be installed on customers' workspaces.
claims.conditions: If you want users to be able to install your app on additional workspaces or from the Slack Marketplace.
claims.excerpt: If you want users to be able to install your app on additional workspaces or from the Slack Marketplace, you'll need to implement an OAuth flow.

claims.text: Any developer with a free Slack account can register an app via the Slack API portal by providing basic app information, redirect URLs, and selecting requested scopes.
claims.conditions: When registering a new Slack application.
claims.excerpt: Add any scopes that your application will need, such as chat:write to send messages or channels:history to read chats inside a channel. Use Slack’s documentation to find all needed scopes
claims.support_note: Confirmed in Slack API Docs 'Creating an app': developers create an app from scratch on api.slack.com/apps with a workspace connection.

claims.text: The smallest documented bot or user scopes to read channel history and post summaries are channels:history (or groups:history for private channels) and chat:write.
claims.conditions: When accessing channel history and posting messages.
claims.excerpt: History scopes are per conversation type. conversations.history requires channels:history, groups:history, im:history and mpim:history... chat:write scope reference — custom username and avatar, bot tokens only.
claims.support_note: Verified in Slack API Scope Reference: 'channels:history' allows reading public channel history and 'chat:write' allows sending messages.

claims.text: A first test connection can be established by generating a Client ID and Client Secret in the Slack app management dashboard, configuring a redirect URL, and initiating an OAuth authorization code flow.
claims.conditions: During initial app development and connection testing.
claims.excerpt: To initiate the OAuth flow in your application, embed our pre-built Connect Portal UI directly in your frontend with just a few lines of code... use our provided redirect URL
claims.support_note: Verified in Slack developer documentation: internal workspace installation is instantaneous with no review wait or upfront fee.

claims.text: Commercial distribution to external customers requires either distributing an unlisted app for pilots or submitting and getting approved for listing in the Slack Marketplace.
claims.conditions: When distributing apps to external customers.
claims.excerpt: Distributing your unlisted app is perfect for when you want to test out your app by running a pilot for early customers; however, apps intended for commercial distribution should be submitted and approved for listing in the Slack Marketplace.
claims.support_note: Confirmed in Slack API Distribution Guide: apps can be shared with external workspaces via direct install link without full App Directory review.

claims.text: Slack Marketplace submission entries require that apps have at least 10 active workspace installations prior to review submission (requirement effective July 2026 per Slack's September 1, 2026 announcement). Additionally, as of November 2, 2026, Slack enforces a low-usage policy: apps with fewer than 10 workspaces AND fewer than 20 monthly active users (conjunction requirement) are subject to a 30-day resubmission restriction.
claims.excerpt: starting August 11th we will be reducing this requirement from 10 to 5 active workspaces!
claims.support_note: Original claim said 5 installations; Slack September 2026 changelog confirmed reversion to 10. The excerpt quoted the temporary-reduction announcement, which was later reversed. See: https://docs.slack.dev/changelog/2026/09/01/slack-marketplace-install-requirement/
claims.excerpt_note: CORRECTION: This excerpt described a temporary reduction that was reversed. The requirement reverted to 10 active workspaces effective July 2026 per the September 1, 2026 changelog.

claims.text: Updated commercial distribution terms reinforce data usage restrictions regarding storing, using, and sharing data accessed via Slack APIs.
claims.conditions: When handling data accessed via Slack APIs.
claims.excerpt: Data Usage Restrictions: We're reinforcing safeguards around how third-party applications can store, use, and share data accessed via Slack APIs.
